steps: Identify the solid (prism, cylinder, cone, sphere, pyramid)
method_card.title: How to Calculate Volume & Surface Area
method_card.content:
Key formulas (given on the exam formula sheet for cones/spheres):

$$\text{Prism volume} = \text{cross-section area} \times \text{length}$$

$$\text{Cylinder: } V = \pi r^2 h \qquad \text{SA} = 2\pi r^2 + 2\pi rh$$

$$\text{Cone: } V = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h \qquad \text{Curved SA} = \pi r l$$

$$\text{Sphere: } V = \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3 \qquad \text{SA} = 4\pi r^2$$

$$\text{Pyramid: } V = \frac{1}{3} \times \text{base area} \times h$$

For compound solids, add or subtract the volumes of simpler shapes. Always check units match.
method_card.example:
Find the volume of a cylinder with radius 4 cm and height 10 cm.

\(V = \pi \times 4^2 \times 10 = 160\pi \approx 502.7\) cm³

gold.display: A sphere has volume \(288\pi\) cm³. Find the radius.

misconceptions._note: Message describes the correct method. Most likely wrong-formula error: student skips multiplying by 3/4 and gets r³ = 288 directly, then r = ∛288 ≈ 6.6.

gold.display: A cone and a cylinder have the same base radius (5 cm) and the same height (12 cm). Find the difference in their volumes to 1 d.p.

misconceptions._note: Message describes the correct method. Most likely wrong-formula error: student forgets the ⅓ for the cone, treats both as cylinders (300π − 300π = 0).

gold.display: A solid hemisphere of radius 4 cm sits on top of a cylinder of radius 4 cm and height 10 cm. Find the total volume to 1 d.p.

misconceptions._note: Message contains an incorrect stored answer (637.7 should be 636.7). Most likely wrong-formula error: student uses full sphere instead of hemisphere — 160π + (4/3)π×64 = 160π + 256π/3 = 736π/3 ≈ 770.7.

gold.display: A sphere has surface area \(100\pi\) cm². Find the radius.

misconceptions._note: Message describes the correct method. Most likely wrong-formula error: student finds r² = 25 correctly but forgets to take the square root and gives 25 as the answer.

gold.display: A frustum is formed by removing a cone of height 4 cm and radius 2 cm from a cone of height 12 cm and radius 6 cm. Find the volume of the frustum to 1 d.p.

misconceptions._note: Message describes the correct method. Most likely wrong-formula error: student forgets to subtract the small cone and uses only the large cone — 144π ≈ 452.4.

bronze.display: Find the volume of a cube with side length 6 cm.

misconceptions._note: Message describes the correct method, not a wrong one. Most typical error (using SA = 6s² = 216) gives the same numerical answer as the volume for s=6, so no deterministic wrong value exists.

bronze.display: A cuboid is 10 cm × 4 cm × 3 cm. Find its volume.

misconceptions._note: Message describes the correct method. Possible wrong answers vary widely (adding dimensions: 17; two-face product: 40; SA of three pairs: 82; full SA: 164). No single dominant wrong answer.

bronze.display: A triangular prism has cross-section area 15 cm² and length 8 cm. Find its volume.

misconceptions._note: Message describes the correct method. Most likely distinct wrong answer: student uses only the cross-section area (15) and forgets to multiply by the length.

bronze.display: A cylinder has radius 3 cm and height 10 cm. Find its volume to 1 d.p.

misconceptions._note: Message describes the correct method. Most common wrong-formula error: student uses diameter (6) instead of radius (3) — V = π × 36 × 10 = 360π ≈ 1131.0.

bronze.display: Find the surface area of a cube with side 5 cm.

misconceptions._note: Message describes the correct method. Most likely wrong answer: student calculates area of one face only (5² = 25).

bronze.display: A cuboid is 8 cm × 3 cm × 2 cm. Find its surface area.

misconceptions._note: Message describes the correct method. Most likely wrong answer: student finds the three distinct face areas (24+16+6 = 46) but forgets to multiply by 2.

bronze.display: A cylinder has radius 4 cm and height 7 cm. Find the volume to 1 d.p.

misconceptions._note: Message describes the correct method. Most common wrong-formula error: student uses diameter (8) instead of radius (4) — V = π × 64 × 7 = 448π ≈ 1407.4.
Message describes the correct method. Most common unit error: student thinks 1 litre = 100 cm³ (confusing with centilitres) and calculates 2.5 × 100 = 250.

silver.display: Find the volume of a sphere with radius 6 cm to 1 d.p.

misconceptions._note: Message describes the correct method. Most common wrong-formula error: student uses the SA formula (4πr²) instead of volume — 4π × 36 = 144π ≈ 452.4.

silver.display: Find the volume of a cone with radius 5 cm and height 12 cm to 1 d.p.

misconceptions._note: Message describes the correct method. Most common wrong-formula error: student forgets the ⅓ factor — V = π × 25 × 12 = 300π ≈ 942.5.

silver.display: A cylinder has volume 500 cm³ and radius 5 cm. Find the height to 1 d.p.

misconceptions._note: Message describes the correct method. Likely wrong-formula error: student divides by r instead of r² — h = 500/(5π) = 100/π ≈ 31.8.

silver.display: Find the curved surface area of a cone with radius 4 cm and slant height 9 cm. Give your answer to 1 d.p.

misconceptions._note: Message describes the correct method. Most likely wrong-formula error: student uses cylinder curved SA formula (2πrl) — 2π × 4 × 9 = 72π ≈ 226.2.

silver.display: Find the surface area of a sphere with radius 3 cm to 1 d.p.

misconceptions._note: DEGENERATE: for r=3, the sphere SA (4πr²=36π) and sphere volume ((4/3)πr³=36π) are numerically identical. No deterministic wrong answer from wrong-formula error — any formula-swap is undetectable.

silver.display: A pyramid has square base 6 cm × 6 cm and height 10 cm. Find its volume.

misconceptions._note: Message describes the correct method. Most common wrong-formula error: student forgets the ⅓ factor — V = 36 × 10 = 360.

silver.display: A hemisphere has radius 8 cm. Find its volume to the nearest whole number.

misconceptions._note: Message describes the correct method. Most common wrong-formula error: student uses the full sphere formula — (4/3)π × 512 = 2048π/3 ≈ 2145.
